subject: reasoning
question:
H, I, J, P, Q, R and S are seated around a round table facing the centre. P sits third to the left of Q. R sits second to the left of S. Q is an immediate neighbour of both J and R. H is not an immediate neighbour of P.

How many people are sitting between J and R when counting from the right of J?
solution:
Given: H, I, J, P, Q, R and S are seated around a round table facing the centre

1) P sits third to the left of Q.

2) R sits second to the left of S.

3) Q is an immediate neighbour of both J and R.

4) H is not an immediate neighbour of P.

After positioning all only one position is left which will be occupied by the only person left i.e. B.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ad8b0da23ce9b53e2f4df08efe12623c376ead17ec134fe4a3a66032f9880925.png] [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ab6d60f0650cedb9d746a9bed22e7d30027111f0a3071d375bfd3cabdeb744bb.png] 

Thus, There are** One **people sitting between J and R when counting from the right of J.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 1".
